regions.breakdown: 大戸屋 (Ootoya) is the name of a popular Japanese restaurant chain specializing in "teishoku" (set meals). The square brackets 「」 are used for quoting names or speech.

regions.original: 前は溝の口にもあった。
regions.translation: It used to be in Mizoguchi too.
regions.romanization: Mae wa Mizoguchi ni mo atta.
regions.breakdown: 前 (mae) means "before" or "previously." は (wa) is a topic particle. 溝の口 (Mizoguchi) is a place name (a district in Kawasaki, Kanagawa). に (ni) is a location particle, "in/at." も (mo) means "also" or "too." あった (atta) is the past tense of ある (aru), "to be" or "to exist."

regions.original: また出来る と いいな。
regions.translation: I hope it can open/be established again.
regions.breakdown: また (mata) means "again." 出来る (dekiru) means "to be able to do," "to be completed," or "to open/be established." と (to) here functions to express a condition or result, leading to the following desire. いい (ii) means "good." な (na) is a sentence-ending particle expressing desire, hope, or a gentle suggestion.

where_youd_see_it: On a sidewalk outside a small shop or home, often used as an informal notice board.
cultural_note: Ootoya (大戸屋) is a well-known chain of Japanese restaurants serving home-style set meals (teishoku). The phrase 'また～といいな' is a common and gentle way to express a wish or hope in Japanese.
